subject: General Awareness
summary: NCERT-level physics, chemistry and biology as they appear in daily life: mirrors and lenses, refraction and sound, friction and electricity; acids, bases, common compounds and separation methods; cells, blood, vitamins, diseases and enzymes; and ecology and environmental protection. DSSSB asks short factual questions (which acid is in orange, image position in a concave mirror, organism causing wheat rust), so clear tables and a few key formulas cover most of the marks.

sections.heading: Light: mirrors, lenses, refraction and the eye
sections.body:
**Concave mirror** (converging): forms real, inverted images except when the object is between the pole P and focus F, where the image is virtual, erect and enlarged. Uses: shaving and dentist's mirrors, reflectors of torches and headlights, solar furnaces. **Convex mirror**: always a virtual, erect, diminished image with a wide field of view, so it is used as a rear-view mirror.

**Convex lens**: object at infinity gives a point-sized real image at F₂; object within F₁ gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image (magnifying glass). **Concave lens**: always virtual, erect, diminished.

**Atmospheric refraction** causes the **twinkling of stars**, the **advanced sunrise and delayed sunset** (about 2 minutes each) and the flattened look of the Sun near the horizon. Planets do not twinkle because they are extended sources. **Scattering** of light makes the sky blue and the sunset red; red is scattered least, so it is used for danger signals. **Total internal reflection** explains the sparkle of diamonds, optical fibres and mirages. A rainbow forms by dispersion, refraction and internal reflection in raindrops. **Malus' law** (I = I₀ cos²θ) describes the intensity of polarised light.

**Human eye**: the **iris** controls the size of the pupil; the lens focuses; the image forms on the **retina** (rods for dim light, cones for colour). **Myopia** (near-sightedness) is corrected with a concave lens, **hypermetropia** with a convex lens, presbyopia with bifocals.

sections.heading: Sound, motion, heat and electricity
sections.body:
**Sound** needs a medium and travels fastest in solids, slower in liquids and slowest in gases (about 343 m/s in air at 20°C). **Loudness depends on amplitude** (large amplitude, loud sound); **pitch depends on frequency** (high frequency, high pitch). Human hearing range: **20 Hz to 20 kHz**; above it is **ultrasound** (bats, SONAR, medical scans), below it **infrasound**. A distinct echo needs a reflecting surface at least about 17 m away.

**Friction**: static friction > sliding (kinetic) friction > rolling friction. That is why wheels and ball bearings reduce friction.

**Newton's laws**: inertia (1st), F = ma (2nd), action and reaction (3rd: recoil of a gun, rocket propulsion). **Pressure = force ÷ area**, so knives are sharpened and bags have wide straps. A ship floats because of buoyancy (Archimedes' principle). Weight on the Moon is about one-sixth of that on Earth; mass is unchanged.

**Heat**: conduction (solids), convection (liquids and gases; sea and land breezes), radiation (no medium needed). Water is densest at **4°C**. Boiling point falls at high altitude; a pressure cooker raises it. Body temperature 37°C = 98.6°F.

**Electricity**: Indian household supply is **220 V AC at 50 Hz**. A **fuse** wire has a low melting point and breaks the circuit on overload. A motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the reverse; a transformer works only on AC. 1 kWh ('one unit') = 3.6 × 10⁶ J.

sections.heading: Acids, bases and common compounds
sections.body:
On the **pH scale**, below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral (pure water) and above 7 is basic. Human blood is slightly basic (about 7.4); the stomach contains hydrochloric acid; tooth decay starts when mouth pH falls below about 5.5. An antacid such as **milk of magnesia** (magnesium hydroxide) neutralises excess stomach acid.

**Bases in use**: sodium hydroxide (caustic soda, soap making), calcium hydroxide (slaked lime, whitewash), magnesium hydroxide (antacid), **ammonium hydroxide (window and glass cleaners)**.

**Alloys**: brass = copper + zinc; bronze = copper + tin; stainless steel = iron + chromium + nickel (+ carbon); solder = tin + lead; amalgam = any alloy of mercury.

**Metals**: **malleability** = can be beaten into sheets; **ductility** = can be drawn into wires; sonority = ringing sound; lustre = shine. Silver is the best conductor; mercury is the only liquid metal at room temperature and bromine the only liquid non-metal. Sodium and potassium are stored in kerosene. Rusting of iron needs both air (oxygen) and water; **galvanisation** coats iron with zinc.

**Fuels**: LPG is mainly butane (with propane); CNG and biogas are mainly methane.

sections.heading: Common names, formulas and separation methods
sections.body: Common-name questions are frequent. Separation methods are asked from NCERT Class 6-9 examples: **threshing** separates grain from stalks; **winnowing** uses wind or blown air to separate lighter husk from heavier grain; **sieving** separates by size; **hand-picking** removes stones; **sedimentation and decantation** let heavier particles settle and pour off the liquid; **filtration** removes insoluble solids; **evaporation** recovers dissolved salt; **distillation** separates miscible liquids with different boiling points; **chromatography** separates dyes in ink; **centrifugation** separates cream from milk; **sublimation** separates camphor, naphthalene or ammonium chloride; a **magnet** separates iron filings.

sections.heading: Cells, blood and the human body
sections.body:
The **cell** is the basic unit of life. **Prokaryotic** cells (bacteria) have no nuclear membrane and usually a single circular chromosome; **eukaryotic** cells have a true nucleus and more than one (linear) chromosome. Organelles: **mitochondria** (powerhouse, ATP), **ribosomes** (protein synthesis), **lysosomes** ('suicide bags'), **chloroplasts** (photosynthesis, plants only); plant cells also have a cellulose cell wall.

**Blood**: **red blood cells** carry oxygen using haemoglobin (made in bone marrow, life about 120 days); **white blood cells** fight germs that enter the body; **platelets** help clotting. Blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner: **O negative** is the universal donor, **AB positive** the universal recipient. Normal blood pressure is about 120/80 mm Hg. The human heart has four chambers.

**Facts**: an adult has **206 bones**; the smallest is the **stapes** (ear) and the longest the **femur**. The largest organ is the **skin**, the largest gland the **liver**. Insulin comes from the pancreas (deficiency causes diabetes); iodine is needed for thyroxine (deficiency causes goitre).

**Breathing organs**: fish - **gills**; earthworm - moist **skin**; frog - skin and lungs; insects - tracheae (spiracles); humans - lungs (alveoli).

**Enzymes**: salivary amylase (starch), pepsin (proteins, stomach), trypsin (proteins, pancreas), lipase (fats); **catalase** breaks hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen. Bile (from the liver) emulsifies fats but contains no enzyme.

sections.heading: Nutrition and diseases
sections.body:
Vitamins **A, D, E and K** are fat-soluble; B and C are water-soluble. Mineral deficiencies: iron - anaemia; iodine - goitre; calcium - weak bones and teeth.

**Diseases by cause**
- **Bacteria**: tuberculosis, cholera, typhoid, tetanus, diphtheria, leprosy, plague, whooping cough.
- **Viruses**: AIDS (HIV), influenza, measles, mumps, polio, rabies, hepatitis, chickenpox, dengue, COVID-19.
- **Protozoa**: malaria (Plasmodium, spread by female Anopheles), amoebic dysentery, kala-azar (Leishmania, sandfly).
- **Fungi**: ringworm, athlete's foot; in plants, **rust of wheat** (Puccinia).
- Vectors: **Aedes** - dengue, chikungunya, Zika; **Culex** - filariasis.

Discoveries: **Edward Jenner** - smallpox vaccine; **Louis Pasteur** - rabies vaccine and pasteurisation; **Alexander Fleming** - penicillin (1928); BCG vaccine protects against tuberculosis. WHO declared smallpox eradicated in 1980.

sections.heading: Environment and ecology
sections.body:
An **ecosystem** has producers (green plants), consumers (herbivores, carnivores) and decomposers (bacteria, fungi). A food chain example: grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → eagle. By the **10% law**, only about a tenth of the energy at one trophic level passes to the next, so the **pyramid of energy is always upright**. **Biomagnification**: non-degradable poisons such as DDT and mercury become more concentrated at higher trophic levels.

**Pollution and its effects**
- Greenhouse gases: carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide, water vapour, CFCs.
- **Ozone** (stratosphere) is depleted by **CFCs**; measured in Dobson units.
- **Acid rain** comes from sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides and damages marble (the Taj Mahal).
- **Bhopal gas tragedy (1984)**: methyl isocyanate. Minamata disease: mercury. Itai-itai: cadmium. Blue-baby syndrome: excess nitrate in water. Fluorosis: excess fluoride.

**Agreements and laws**: Ramsar Convention on wetlands (1971); Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972; Project Tiger (1973); Montreal Protocol on ozone-depleting substances (1987); Environment (Protection) Act 1986; Earth Summit, Rio (1992); Kyoto Protocol (1997); Paris Agreement (2015).

**Conservation**: **in-situ** (national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves) and **ex-situ** (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks). India has parts of four global biodiversity hotspots: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). The **Chipko movement** (1973, Uttarakhand) involved hugging trees to stop felling.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: A household uses four 60 W bulbs for 5 hours a day for 30 days. Electricity costs ₹5 per unit. Find the bill.
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Total power = 4 × 60 = 240 W = 0.24 kW.
Step 2: Hours = 5 × 30 = 150 h.
Step 3: Energy = 0.24 × 150 = 36 kWh = 36 units.
Step 4: Bill = 36 × 5 = **₹180**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: A boy claps near a cliff and hears the echo after 2 s. Speed of sound = 340 m/s. How far is the cliff?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: In 2 s sound travels 340 × 2 = 680 m.
Step 2: This is the distance to the cliff and back.
Step 3: Distance = 680 ÷ 2 = **340 m**.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: Convert a body temperature of 98.6°F to Celsius.
Practice: In a food chain grass → deer → tiger, the grass fixes 20,000 J of energy. Using the 10% law, how much energy reaches the tiger?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: Grass to deer: 10% of 20,000 = 2,000 J.
Step 2: Deer to tiger: 10% of 2,000 = **200 J**.
This loss at each step is why food chains rarely have more than 4-5 levels.

workedExamples.problem: Practice: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where is the image and what is its size?
workedExamples.solution:
Step 1: R = 2f = 30 cm, so the object is at u = −30 cm.
Step 2: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/(−15) − 1/(−30) = −2/30 + 1/30 = −1/30, so v = −30 cm.
Step 3: Magnification m = −v/u = −(−30)/(−30) = −1.
Answer: the image is **at C (30 cm in front of the mirror), real, inverted and of the same size**.

pitfalls: Calling amla a rich source of vitamin A; it is famous for vitamin C. Carrot, mango and papaya are vitamin A sources.
Saying higher frequency gives lower pitch; higher frequency means higher pitch.
Ranking sliding friction above static friction; static > sliding > rolling.
Placing the image at C when the object is at infinity; it forms at F.
Thinking wheat rust is bacterial; it is caused by a fungus.
Thinking earthworms have lungs; they breathe through moist skin.
Saying the lens or cornea controls the size of the pupil; the iris does, while the lens focuses light.
Forgetting to halve the distance in echo problems.
quickRevision: Concave mirror: object at infinity → image at F; object at C → image at C, same size.
Convex lens, object at infinity → image at F₂, highly diminished.
Atmospheric refraction: twinkling stars, advanced sunrise and delayed sunset.
Loudness ∝ amplitude; pitch ∝ frequency; hearing 20 Hz-20 kHz.
Orange and lemon: citric acid; curd: lactic; vinegar: acetic; ant sting: formic.
Ductility = drawn into wires; malleability = beaten into sheets.
Winnowing separates lighter husk using wind.
WBCs fight germs; RBCs carry oxygen; platelets clot blood.
Fish breathe through gills; earthworms through skin.
Vitamin C deficiency: scurvy; vitamin D: rickets; vitamin A: night blindness.
Montreal Protocol (1987) protects the ozone layer.
